libm_flavour_sensitivity.question: does the single-world PUCT search DISCRIMINATE the G0 libm choice?
libm_flavour_sensitivity.method: Rust-vs-Rust: production config (exp_fma + glibc_fma tanh) vs each alternative flavour, same positions, compare chosen action and every root child's (N, W) raw bits
libm_flavour_sensitivity.finding: The search is NEARLY BLIND to the libm flavour at this scale: the np.exp site shows 0/720 and math.tanh only 2/720, with the chosen action never changing. G3-green therefore does NOT re-prove the G0 libm finding -- G0's 10^8 fuzz remains the only thing pinning it. Load-bearing for P7: an Android/bionic build with the WRONG flavour could pass a search-identity gate of this size and still be wrong (the same trap G0 flagged as 'msun_fma passes the corpus while failing the fuzz'). Note msun_fma is again the flavour that hides.

legal_move_cache.question: is the repr-keyed legal-mask cache ever serving a DIFFERENT board (the Phase-0.3 rotation-collision hazard) inside a single-world search?
legal_move_cache.finding: Within ONE fresh-tree search the cache is pure SAME-BOARD memoization: Python hits exactly once per expansion (the second get_valid_moves on the identical Board object -- hits == misses == expansions), and 0 cross-board collisions were logged. The Rust side computes each node's mask once and reuses it, so it takes 0 hits by construction. The Phase-0.3 collision hazard is therefore NOT REACHABLE in the single-world PUCT path; the Rust cache is faithful but semantically inert here. It may become reachable in P4/tree-reuse paths, which is why it is kept.

transposition_alias_path.question: is the child_canon / child_aliases / prior_bonus machinery (rotationally symmetric tiles collapsing to ONE child object) actually exercised by the gate corpus?
transposition_alias_path.method: walk every node of the Python tree after each search
transposition_alias_path.finding: Exercised, not vacuous: 2.3% of nodes carry at least one alias even at only 200 sims, and 211 prior-bonus folds fired. Both affect PUCT directly, so the gate's bit-equality covers them.
